subject: Post-call: Private/VPC performance & SLO follow-up (latency, network path, streaming)

Subject: Post-call: Private/VPC performance & SLO follow-up (latency, network path, streaming)

Thanks for the time today — good discussion. Quick recap + action items from Redwood side and a few asks for your network/ops team so we can validate whether Private (VPC) deployment meets Acme's latency/throughput targets.

Call highlights:
- Target SLOs: p95 end-to-end request latency <= 120ms for chat completions (non-streaming), steady-state throughput target ~150 req/s for 4 concurrent models, burst to 400 req/s. Streaming requirements: chunk latency <= 60ms typical (token-level streaming).
- Deployment model: Private inference nodes inside your VPC (we discussed Transit Gateway / Direct Connect options) with optional on-prem package if needed.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 controls, KMS integration for keys.

Action items (we'll take first two):
1) Redwood: provide a short SLO checklist and example network/security rules (attached: redwood-slo-checklist.xlsx).
2) Redwood: share recommended ports and NAT/firewall settings for VPC-hosted inference (we'll attach network diagram template).
3) Acme: please share current network path between your app tier and the proposed inference subnet (traceroute/MTR from representative app instance, NAT gateway path if using public egress).
4) Acme: confirm whether you'll use Direct Connect/PrivateLink, Transit Gateway peering, or site-to-site VPN for routing; include expected egress bandwidth and any per-connection CPU/packet filtering appliances.
5) Acme NetworkOps: if you have a topology diagram (internal firewall rules, IDS appliances, asymmetric routing), please send — we need to estimate added latency and jitter.

For engineering validation we typically ask for:
- traceroute/mtr from 2 regions (app nodes) to a test endpoint we provide (we can spin up an endpoint in your VPC or you can run to our public test host)
- average and p95 RTT on internal network hops, and MTU/path MTU if you have PMTU enforcement
- any known packet inspection/termination that can add >5-10ms per request

I copied Laura (solutions) to coordinate scheduling of a short network troubleshooting session with your NetOps.

Next steps: please reply with the network attachments/notes or let us know times for a 30-min NetOps call this week.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Sanjay — good questions. Short answers and proposed measurement plan:

- SLO scope: the p95 <= 120ms we discussed is end-to-end as visible to your app tier (so includes TLS handshake amortization if not reused; we recommend persistent connections to minimize that cost). For engineering validation we break it down into: app->inference network RTT, inference node processing time (token generation latency), and any egress/ingress NAT/firewall overhead.

- Measurement plan:
  1) Acme runs traceroute/MTR to the test endpoint we will provide inside your VPC (or to our probe if you prefer).
  2) We'll provide a small load-script (curl/wrk script) to run short streaming and non-streaming requests at low QPS so we can measure chunk latency and p95 without saturating backend.
  3) Aditya and Dev (cc'd) will review your topology and advise whether additional kernel tuning or keepalive settings (Nginx/proxy) are recommended.

Aditya/dev — can you confirm the recommended TCP keepalive, HTTP/2 SETTINGS (if using gRPC/HTTP2), and any MTU advice for token streaming workloads? Also flag anything else we should ask Acme NetOps for (e.g., number of NAT SNAT ports if they use a large pod scale).

I'll hold a 30-min slot tomorrow for NetOps review if that works for your team.

Thanks,
Marissa

Looping in engineering notes — short checklist we typically use for Private/VPC low-latency streaming workloads:

- TCP keepalive: enable and tune to 30s probes, with 3 probes before teardown. This avoids silent half-open connections for long-lived streams.
- HTTP/2 or gRPC: prefer HTTP/2 with flow control tuned; gRPC with client-side flow control works well for chunked token streaming.
- TLS: use session resumption / keepalive to avoid full handshake for each request.
- MTU: avoid PMTU blackhole — recommend standard 1500 unless you have Jumbo frames configured end-to-end. If you do use Jumbo, confirm across path.
- NAT SNAT port exhaustion: for large fanout from many ephemeral clients, ensure SNAT port capacity or use egress NAT gateways with source preservation.
- Packet inspection: app-level DPI appliances can add 5–25ms jitter per packet depending on throughput; identify if any inline appliances are in the path.
- Bandwidth: for token streaming, plan for ~12–20 KB/s per active stream (depends on token size/encoding); multiply by concurrency to estimate egress.

For measurements, please capture p50/p95/p99 for RTT at the app hop and also record chunk latency (time from request send to first token and subsequent token intervals) for streaming requests. If you can provide an ROI for your load (typical QPS + concurrency distribution) we can simulate a realistic profile.

Happy to join the NetOps call — propose Wed 2026-06-17 09:00-09:30 PT.
